title: Contributing to move2utils
text: move2utils developed MPCDF GitLab (https://gitlab.mpcdf.mpg.de/anenvi/r-packages/move2utils), source truth; GitHub repository public release. welcome : Report bugs / request features opening issue , ideally minimal reproducible example bundled data (inst/extdata/ move2 example data). Propose changes via pull request. development happens GitLab, accepted PRs ported flow back next release, authorship preserved. move2utils intentionally minimal scope: utilities operate directly move2 objects. Proposals outside scope likely better placed package. New functionality come tests roxygen2 docs; please keep R CMD check green.

title: Getting started: cleaning a track with move2utils
text: Almost every GPS satellite track contains bad locations: fix wrong place, brief satellite-geometry error, tag switched fitted. usually tiny fraction data, real damage — one location far place inflates every speed compute distorts home ranges. Cleaning first step movement analyses. definitive list correct outliers. outlier judgement location implausible keep; obvious, others borderline. move2utils try find perfect set. flags conspicuous errors reliably, leaves believable data alone, shows judgement stays . Always plot result check . automatic cleaner trusted blind. mt_clean_track() cleaning combining four independent checks (path position, --back spikes, unusual movement, speed) single decision. vignette covers one-call workflow, check finer control.

title: Getting started: cleaning a track with move2utils

title: Getting started: cleaning a track with move2utils
text: mt_clean_track() runs four checks turn, decides locations flag, removes groups bad locations form isolated blocks, iterates nothing new flagged. default returns cleaned track.  messages function narrating decisions; figure shows kept track removed locations marked. Check plot: removed points match pointed? decision made. four checks occasionally fires good data (real sharp turn, genuine fast burst), cleaner simply count votes. weighs strongly check distrusts location flags combined evidence positive either two checks agree one overwhelmingly sure. catches clear errors single check happens see, without -cleaning believable data. rule default (consensus = "evidence_corroborated"); can change via consensus = — earlier behaviour "class_aware", "strict", "majority", "speed_trusted", "weighted_evidence", "" "custom" also available (see ?mt_flag_consensus). see check caught , set remove = FALSE: every location kept ones removed labelled. columns flagged_by_bridge (path position), flagged_by_detour (--back), flagged_by_prob (unusual movement), flagged_by_speed (speed), together flag_iteration block_id, record provenance flag. error_class column names rule caused flag (e.g. clear --back spike, impossible speed, membership removed block) — see vignette("OUTLIER_2_diagnose_clean_track", package = "move2utils") taxonomy. Errors also come groups: run fake locations spoof, cluster stuck one wrong place. cleaner detects locations forming block cut real trajectory removes whole block, just edges.

what: When to supply a physiological speed cap
title: Getting started: cleaning a track with move2utils
text: default v_max = NULL, speed check infers plausible cap track . safe species, known limit: long, internally consistent error clusters (typical GPS spoofs multi-hour position jumps) small internal step speeds stand edges. single fixed physiological cap, applied repeatedly nothing removed, dissolves cleanly. block-detection step also uses v_max decide locations connected. removes block data show expected “trajectory plus isolated clusters” shape; inferred cap sits inside species’ normal speed range, removing blocks cut real trajectory, step declined automatically (decision printed narration). enable fast-flying species, give physiological cap via v_max = (mass, mode) route . v_max supplied, mt_clean_track() first peels locations cap convergence (mt_peel_speed()), runs remaining checks survives. mt_suggest_speed_cap() diagnostic helper: reports data-driven candidates warns disagree, deliberately pick v_max .
code: ## a large eagle sustains roughly 30 m/s, a stork roughly 50 m/s clean <- mt_clean_track(track, v_max = 30) mt_suggest_speed_cap(track)

what: A principled default from body mass and locomotor mode
title: Getting started: cleaning a track with move2utils
text: Without published speed cap, can derive one body mass locomotor mode using Hirt et al. (2017) scaling law. v_phys_estimate(mass, mode) returns predicted maximum sustained speed m/s confidence interval; mt_clean_track() accepts (mass, mode) pair directly. mt_suggest_speed_cap() takes arguments overlays allometric prediction step-speed distribution alongside user value, empirical break, allometric prediction, supplied v_max appear one plot. Disagreement informative: empirical break well allometric prediction signals contamination; one well within-distribution structure (behavioural states, gait changes) cut. locomotor mode uncertain (stork flies walks, seal swims walks), pass mass alone diagnostic shows three mode-specific lines.
code: v_phys_estimate(mass = 5, mode = "flying")            # eagle-class, printed with CI clean <- mt_clean_track(track, mass = 5, mode = "flying") mt_suggest_speed_cap(track, mass = 5, mode = "flying", v_max = 30) mt_suggest_speed_cap(track, mass = 1)

title: Getting started: cleaning a track with move2utils
text: check also exported , inspecting single signal building pipeline. Path position — mt_flag_outliers_bridge(). Scores location far sits temporal neighbours place , scaled width depends timestamps — bad location inflate tolerance. directional variant separates along-track across-track deviation classifies kind error. See vignette("OUTLIER_4_outlier_bridge", package = "move2utils"). Unusual movement — mt_flag_outliers(). Scores location unusual step length turn relative animal’s movement, catching kinematically implausible fixes geometry alone miss. threshold_type = "gap" (default) finds break log-probability tail; "entropy" conservative; "significance" "percentile" older z-score quantile rules. Speed — mt_flag_speed_cap(). Flags steps whose implied speed exceeds threshold. threshold data-driven default (auto); pass threshold_type = "hard" v_max fixed cap, mt_peel_speed(x, v_max) iterative peel dissolves coherent clusters. --back check mt_flag_outliers_detour(); rule combines four one decision mt_flag_consensus().

br <- mt_flag_outliers_bridge(cpf_a, plot = FALSE) #> Input is in longitude/latitude.  Auto-projecting to a local AEQD for Euclidean bridge math; output is returned in the original CRS. #> Running bridge-residual detection (method = combined) on 1748 locations... #>   Iter 1: flagged 6 (break at eta = 1591.91 / eta_perp = 406.83). #>   Iter 2: flagged 7 (break at eta = 1472.59 / eta_perp = 56.83). #>   Iter 3: flagged 7 (break at eta = 1254.78 / eta_perp = 679.59). #> === 20 outliers (1.14% of 1748) === cat("path-position flagged:", sum(br$is_outlier), "
") #> path-position flagged: 20 pr <- mt_flag_outliers(cpf_a, plot = FALSE) #> Input is in longitude/latitude.  Auto-projecting to a local AEQD for Euclidean prob math; output is returned in the original CRS. #> Calculating movement metrics... #> ACF-derived alpha: 0.139 (r_speed=0.817, r_angvel=0.024) #> Calculating probability distributions... #> Note: step-length range/IQR = 8233 is extreme; #>   teleport-class GPS errors are better handled by #>   mt_filter_gps_quality() (drop fixes with <5 satellites) #>   and mt_flag_outliers_bridge() (geometric, leverage-immune). #>   step_transform = "log" is available but can hide #>   physiologically-plausible joint turn/step outliers. #> Calculating joint probabilities... #> Identifying outliers... #>  #> 3 locations (0.2%) have NA probabilities --will be kept. #> === 5 outliers (0.29% of 1748) === cat("unusual-movement flagged:", sum(pr$is_outlier), "
") #> unusual-movement flagged: 5 sc <- mt_flag_speed_cap(cpf_a, plot = FALSE) #> Auto-cap landed at 60.1 m/s -- above 55.0 m/s (universal sustained-speed bound, not species-specific). Supply `(mass, mode)` to `mt_clean_track()` (or pass a hard `v_max`) for a principled physiological cap.  See `?v_phys_estimate`. #> Speed cap: 60.1041 m/s (auto) -- 23 fix(es) flagged. what: A run that needs attention — Pettstadt1, a juvenile white stork
title: Diagnosing an mt_clean_track run
text: Pettstadt1 juvenile white stork (~3 kg) 48k GPS fixes spanning two summers one autumn migration. clean , run diagnostic result. flag fraction high — genuine GPS errors produce stork. Time ask diagnostic happened.  function prints concerns found renders six panels.
code: pet <- mt_read(system.file("extdata/Pettstadt1-14053.csv.gz",                               package = "move2utils")) pet <- pet[!st_is_empty(pet), ] pet <- mt_filter_unique(pet, criterion = "first") pet <- dplyr::arrange(pet, mt_track_id(pet), mt_time(pet)) res_pet <- mt_clean_track(pet, mass = 3, mode = "flying",                             plot = FALSE, remove = FALSE,                             silent = TRUE,                             max_flag_fraction = 0.5) cat(sprintf("Pettstadt1: %d / %d flagged (%.2f%%)\n",             sum(res_pet$is_outlier), nrow(res_pet),             100 * mean(res_pet$is_outlier))) #> Pettstadt1: 6504 / 48239 flagged (13.48%) diag <- mt_diagnose_clean_track(res_pet) #> === mt_diagnose_clean_track: concerns flagged === #> Panel 1: 3 substantive modes detected at 0.01, 0.95, 8.51 m/s -- bimodal behaviour. The per-fix detectors threshold against a single distribution; consider state-conditional analysis or filtering to one mode before cleaning. #> Panel 2: sustained band of elevated flag rate detected -- this is the migration-over-flagging signature. Consider filtering that window or running it through state-conditional analysis.

title: Diagnosing an mt_clean_track run
text: Whichever consensus rule decides flags, mt_clean_track() labels flagged fix one error_class, diagnostic (inspection) reads vocabulary every time. categories : consensus — least three four checks agreed. geometric_spike — path-position --back checks agreed (classic --back spike). state_anomaly — geometric check plus speed cap. kinematic_confluence — geometric check plus unusual-movement check. block — part connected group fixes cut real trajectory removed unit (spoof / multi-hour-jump case). physiological — removed hard physiological speed cap (v_max / mass + mode path). state_transition_buffered — flag near behavioural-state boundary buffer downgraded, can tell genuine errors edge--state artefacts. labels computed independently consensus rule, switching default evidence_corroborated class_aware, strict, majority, rule changes fixes flagged, never flagged fix named.

text: mt_clean_track() runs four checks — path position (mt_flag_outliers_bridge()), --back spikes (mt_flag_outliers_detour()), unusual movement (mt_flag_outliers()), speed (mt_flag_speed_cap()). one compares every location single distribution: bridge residuals, detour ratios, movement probabilities, step speeds. works animal moves one consistent way. breaks animal several behaviours different kinematics — resting perch, soaring, active flight, migration glides. behaviour adds peak distribution, single threshold choose two bad options: cut peaks, -flags smaller behaviour, cut beyond largest peak, misses smaller behaviour’s outliers. Neither right. fix split track behaviour clean piece , every check sees single peak can find outlier tail relative one behaviour.

code: library(move2)  ## Per-fix step speed in m/s, via move2's helper. v <- as.numeric(suppressWarnings(mt_speed(x, units = "m/s")))  ## Smooth it so a single bad fix does not flip the label around it. v_smooth <- stats::filter(v, rep(1/9, 9), sides = 2, circular = FALSE)  ## Cut at a valley reported by mt_diagnose_clean_track() (~ 1 m/s for ## stork-class species; species- and study-specific in practice). state <- ifelse(is.na(v_smooth) | v_smooth > 1,  "active", "stationary")  x_clean <- mt_clean_track(x, v_max = 50, state = state)

Compare -state baseline: clean ground-truth data two similar. real multi-behaviour track split call usually catches outliers pooled call misses (smaller behaviour’s tail) avoids -flagging body smaller behaviour. calls use default flag rule (consensus = "evidence_corroborated"): check’s evidence weighed common scale, location flagged combined evidence positive either least two checks agree --back check alone overwhelmingly sure. state = split changes check sees, flags combined. error_class column, names rule behind flag, filled regardless consensus rule. rules available via consensus = — including earlier "class_aware", plus "strict", "majority", "speed_trusted", "weighted_evidence", "" "custom" (see ?mt_flag_consensus).
code: library(move2) library(move2utils)  m <- read.csv(gzfile(system.file("extdata",                                   "synthetic_tracks.csv.gz",                                   package = "move2utils")),               stringsAsFactors = FALSE) m$timestamp <- as.POSIXct(m$timestamp, tz = "UTC") mA <- mt_as_move2(m[m$individual.local.identifier == "CPF_A", ],                   coords = c("location.long", "location.lat"),                   time_column = "timestamp",                   track_id_column = "individual.local.identifier",                   crs = 4326)  ## Made-up two-state label: first half "rest", second half "flight". state <- c(rep("rest",   floor(nrow(mA) / 2)),            rep("flight", nrow(mA) - floor(nrow(mA) / 2)))  out <- mt_clean_track(mA, v_max = 30, state = state,                        plot = FALSE, remove = FALSE, silent = TRUE)  table(state, flagged = out$is_outlier) #>         flagged #> state    FALSE TRUE #>   flight   851   23 #>   rest     868    6 out_pooled <- mt_clean_track(mA, v_max = 30,                               plot = FALSE, remove = FALSE, silent = TRUE) sum(out_pooled$is_outlier) #> [1] 29 sum(out$is_outlier) #> [1] 29

title: Bridge-residual outlier detection and error-morphology classification
text: fix projected coordinates p_i time t_i, neighbours -1 +1 define Brownian-bridge expectation m_i = α p_{-1} + (1 − α) p_{+1}, α = Δt₂ / (Δt₁ + Δt₂) Δt₁ = t_i − t_{-1} Δt₂ = t_{+1} − t_i. residual r_i = p_i − m_i. scaled bridge’s standard-deviation width, w_i = √(Δt₁ · Δt₂ / (Δt₁ + Δt₂)). bridge score η_i = ||r_i|| / w_i. noted , w_i depends timestamps, never positions, outlier inflate denominator.

title: Bridge-residual outlier detection and error-morphology classification
text: method = "isotropic" uses plain residual magnitude. General-purpose; answers “fix far ?”. method = "directional" splits residual along local travel direction parallel part (η_para, along-track) perpendicular part (η_perp, across-track). flags η_perp alone, value (η_para, η_perp) pair — tells kind error flag . method = "combined" (default) applies threshold scores flags fix either one trips. check borrows bridge-mean construction dynamic Brownian bridge (dBBMM) perpendicular split dynamic bivariate Gaussian bridge (dBGB), deliberately use variance-estimation step — avoids leverage problem. See mt_dbbmm_variance() / mt_dbgb_variance() full dynamic models.

title: Bridge-residual outlier detection and error-morphology classification
text: read plane: Near diagonal — η_para ≈ η_perp. Scatter directions; classic jitter-type error. diagonal (high η_para, low η_perp) — along-track jumps. Ghost reports, clock glitches, GNSS fold-back. diagonal (low η_para, high η_perp) — across-track drift. Typical multipath, reflective environments, constellation changes bias one axis. isotropic directional flag sets can look quite different real data even though come residual: isotropic score answers far, directional split answers way. Together separate error types one check lump.

title: Troubleshooting: when mt_clean_track() doesn't do what you want
text: default rule, evidence_corroborated, flags location checks’ combined evidence positive either two checks agree --back check alone overwhelming. Two alternatives worth knowing, set via consensus =: "class_aware" — previous default. Stricter requiring corroboration, slightly better coherent clusters; use default removes near-bulk point wanted kept. "weighted_evidence" — sensitive: flags positive combined evidence alone, without corroboration safeguard. Use default misses conspicuous point, accepting false alarms. fine control, standalone mt_flag_consensus() returns combined_evidence column — single number per location summarising strongly checks distrust . Sorting , thresholding , gives one-dial sensitivity control without changing detector.
code: clean <- mt_clean_track(track, consensus = "weighted_evidence")

what: Do not bridge across long gaps
title: Dynamic Brownian bridge UDs (dBBMM)
text: missing satellite pass leaves long time lag otherwise adjacent fixes. Integrating bridge across gap smears probability across regions animal never visited. fix mark locations “interest” variance object rasterising; UD integration skip . remove block fixes open one long (~26 h) gap. Leroy’s first 500 fixes also already contain several natural overnight gaps, masking every segment longer 300 minutes cleans — injected gap included. Compare UD without mask:  difference usually visible low-density ribbon connecting two sub-tracks; masking removes .
code: ## remove a block of fixes to open a long (~26 h) gap keep <- setdiff(seq_len(nrow(leroy)), 200:260) leroy_gap <- leroy[keep, ]  var_gap <- mt_dbbmm_variance(   leroy_gap, location_error = 20,   window_size = 31, margin = 11 ) #> Input is in longitude/latitude.  Auto-projecting to a local AEQD CRS for dynamic Brownian-bridge variance estimation; distances and variances are in metres.  ## the UD with no gap masking — probability bleeds across the gap ud_bleed <- mt_dbbmm_ud(var_gap, location_error = 20, raster = 100,                          verbose = FALSE)  ## mask out locations whose following segment exceeds 300 minutes lag_gap <- as.numeric(mt_time_lags(leroy_gap, units = "min")) var_gap$interest[which(lag_gap > 300)] <- FALSE  ud_masked <- mt_dbbmm_ud(var_gap, location_error = 20, raster = 100,                           verbose = FALSE)  ## for better visualization plotting the cumulative volume UD par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) terra::plot(ud_volume(ud_bleed),  main = "unmasked: bleeds across gap") terra::plot(ud_volume(ud_masked), main = "masked: clean")

text: signature mirrors dBBMM. mt_dbgb_variance() returns S3 object holding parallel perpendicular standard deviations; mt_motion_variance() extracts data.frame columns para orth. quick comparison two dimensions time tells whether animal directional. ratio para / orth > 1 indicates elongation along direction travel.
code: var_dbgb <- mt_dbgb_variance(   leroy,   location_error = 20,   window_size    = 31,   margin         = 11 ) #> Input is in longitude/latitude.  Auto-projecting to a local AEQD CRS for dynamic directional Brownian-bridge variance estimation; distances and variances are in metres.  ## per-location directional variances v_df <- mt_motion_variance(var_dbgb) summary(v_df) #>       para             orth         #>  Min.   :   0.0   Min.   :   0.00   #>  1st Qu.: 211.1   1st Qu.:  45.92   #>  Median :2665.5   Median : 611.22   #>  Mean   :2272.7   Mean   :1427.74   #>  3rd Qu.:3500.0   3rd Qu.:2292.49   #>  Max.   :9634.7   Max.   :7443.30   #>  NAs    :21       NAs    :21 time_days <- as.numeric(mt_time(leroy) - mt_time(leroy)[1], units = "days") plot(time_days, v_df$para, type = "l", col = "steelblue", lwd = 1.5,      ylim = c(0, max(v_df, na.rm = TRUE)),      xlab = "time (days since start)", ylab = "variance (m^2)",      main = "parallel vs perpendicular variance") lines(time_days, v_df$orth, col = "firebrick", lwd = 1.5) legend("topright", c("parallel", "perpendicular"),        col = c("steelblue", "firebrick"), lwd = 1.5, bty = "n")

what: Approach B — burst around each gap
title: Gap-aware UDs: excluding long-gap segments from dBBMM/dBGB
text: individual runs gaps unit analysis — e.g. contrasting pre- post-denning space use, treating nightly foray UD, pairing dBGB run-level directional summary — wrap run composite track_id. Denning segments occupy (two-point) bursts dropped window_size filter. collapse per-run stack single “active-space” UD, weight run duration sum: Use location-count weighting (number locations per run) instead duration time run spans confounded sampling-rate changes. bursting idiom works identically mt_dbgb_variance() / mt_dbgb_ud(). dBGB particularly informative : per-run parallel/perpendicular ratios mt_motion_variance() distinguish commuting-style runs (parallel ≫ perpendicular) foraging-style runs (parallel ≈ perpendicular), typically reason one wants runs separated rather collapsed first place.
code: ## burst_ix increments each time a long gap is crossed; ## a location is assigned to the burst that contains its arrival. is_long_gap_in <- c(FALSE, head(lag_hours, -1) > threshold_h) is_long_gap_in[is.na(is_long_gap_in)] <- FALSE burst_ix       <- cumsum(is_long_gap_in)  leroy_b <- leroy |>   mutate(     burst_id = sprintf("%s__run%02d", mt_track_id(leroy), burst_ix)   ) leroy_b <- mt_set_track_id(leroy_b, "burst_id")  ## drop runs too short to fit the window; ## with window_size = 31 the minimum is 31, but 40 leaves a small margin. min_run <- 40 short   <- names(which(table(mt_track_id(leroy_b)) < min_run)) leroy_b <- leroy_b[!mt_track_id(leroy_b) %in% short, ]  table(mt_track_id(leroy_b)) #>  #> M1__run00 M1__run02 M1__run04 M1__run05 M1__run06 M1__run10 M1__run11 M1__run13  #>        60        51        46       132        40        47       112        48  #> M1__run14 M1__run16 M1__run17 M1__run18  #>        53        59        50        46 var_list <- mt_dbbmm_variance(   leroy_b,   location_error = 25,   window_size    = 31,   margin         = 11 )  ## per-run UDs rastered on a common grid stk <- mt_dbbmm_ud(var_list, location_error = 25, raster = 100, ext = 0.5) names(stk) terra::plot(stk) durations <- vapply(var_list, function(v) {   diff(range(v$track_data$time_mins))    # minutes }, numeric(1)) w <- durations / sum(durations)  ud_active <- sum(stk * w) ud_active <- ud_active / sum(terra::values(ud_active), na.rm = TRUE) terra::plot(ud_active, main = "Duration-weighted active-space UD")

code: ## Given a list of UDs (or a multi-layer SpatRaster) on a common grid: uds_list <- list(day = ud_day, night = ud_night)                # or split  stk <- terra::rast(uds_list)                                     # stack stk <- stk / terra::global(stk, "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[, 1]        # renormalise names(stk) <- names(uds_list) library(move2) library(dplyr) library(sf) library(terra) library(move2utils)  fishers <- mt_read(mt_example()) fishers <- fishers[!st_is_empty(fishers), ]  two <- filter_track_data(fishers, .track_id = c("F3", "M3")) ## keep each individual to its first 500 fixes for a fast build two <- two |>   dplyr::group_by(mt_track_id(two)) |>   dplyr::slice_head(n = 500) |>   dplyr::ungroup() ## The UD functions accept any CRS, but here we deliberately project to a ## metric grid: the EMD default ground metric is Euclidean (and overlap ## metrics compare cells), which only makes sense on equal-area cells. ## On a lon/lat grid you would pass gc = TRUE to emd() instead (see below). two_p <- st_transform(two, mt_aeqd_crs(two))  stk <- mt_dbbmm_ud(   two_p,   location_error = 25,   window_size    = 31,   margin         = 11,   raster         = 100,   ext            = 1.25 ) names(stk) #> [1] "F3" "M3"

title: Corridor detection
text: typical context migratory commuting animal travels two (several) regions via recognisable routes. Within routes, successive segments point way traversed speed; elsewhere track animal forages rests slow, directionally inconsistent speeds. Corridor detection asks: segments track belong route, belong foraging / resting stretches end?

title: Corridor detection
text: segment track, compute speed azimuth. Build search circle centred segment midpoint radius equal half segment length. Collect segment midpoints inside circle. Compute circular variance pseudo-azimuths ((2 * azimuth) mod 2π, azimuths radians) within neighbourhood — doubling lets two animals walking corridor opposite directions count consistent. segment flagged corridor () speed least speed_threshold, (b) neighbourhood’s circular variance circvar_threshold, (c) neighbourhood contains least min_segments qualifying neighbours, must outnumber non-qualifying ones.

title: Corridor detection
text: function works CRS: longitude/latitude projected. Longlat input reprojected internally local azimuthal-equidistant projection (via move2::mt_aeqd_crs()) just buffer--index step; result added back input original CRS. Multi-track input handled track--track natively, via move2::mt_segments() — cross-track segments ever created.

title: Corridor detection
text: speed_threshold (m/s) circvar_threshold (dimensionless, [0, 1]) user-supplied numbers. leave NULL function falls back within-object quantiles (0.75 segment speeds; 0.25 valid circular variances) warns, naming resolved numeric. warning intentional: within-object quantile defines “fast” “directionally consistent” relative animal, convenient single-track exploration makes corridor maps different individuals incomparable. comparable corridors across individuals populations, compute thresholds pooled cohort pass numbers.

title: Corridor detection
text: Five columns added input move2 (length nrow(leroy)): corridor — factor levels "corridor" "corridor". corridor_speed — per-segment speed (m/s); NA last row track row started empty. corridor_azimuth — per-segment azimuth (degrees); NA likewise. corridor_circvar — circular variance pseudo-azimuths within segment’s neighbourhood; NA neighbourhoods size < 2. corridor_n_neighbours — number segments found within search radius.
code: library(move2) library(sf) library(move2utils)  fishers <- mt_read(mt_example()) ## drop empty geometries up front; mt_corridor() would otherwise emit ## a one-line inform notice and NA-pad them in the output, but several ## downstream sf/move2 calls in this vignette (e.g. mt_segments() for ## plotting) require non-empty points throughout. fishers <- fishers[!st_is_empty(fishers), ] leroy   <- filter_track_data(fishers, .track_id = "M1") st_crs(leroy)$input #> [1] "EPSG:4326" ## defaults: within-object quantile fallback fires for both thresholds out <- mt_corridor(leroy) #> Warning: `speed_threshold` not supplied; using within-object 0.75 quantile of #> segment speed = 0.2813 m/s. For cross-individual or cross-population #> comparability, supply an explicit value. #> Warning: `circvar_threshold` not supplied; using within-object 0.25 quantile of #> valid circular variance = 0.2855. For cross-individual or cross-population #> comparability, supply an explicit value. table(out$corridor) #>  #>     corridor not corridor  #>           28          891

text: mt_interpolate() supports three use patterns.

what: A. Regular time cadence via an interval string
title: Interpolating and thinning trajectories
text: "5 mins" string passed lubridate::floor_date(), can use interval format accepts ("30 secs", "2 hours", "1 day", …). max_time_lag policy gaps: original lag longer cutoff bridged; output track break rather dense string interpolated points across gap.
code: ## one fix per five minutes, refusing to bridge gaps longer than 1 h leroy_5min <- mt_interpolate(   leroy,   time         = "5 mins",   max_time_lag = as.difftime(1, units = "hours") ) nrow(leroy); nrow(leroy_5min) #> [1] 300 #> [1] 1893 summary(mt_time_lags(leroy_5min, units = "min")) #>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.     NAs  #> 0.09997 4.45000 5.00000 4.20965 5.00000 5.00000       1

what: B. Interpolate at a specific set of timestamps
title: Interpolating and thinning trajectories
text: Setting omit = TRUE returns requested timestamps discards originals.

title: Interpolating and thinning trajectories
text: question “give ~one fix per 45 min” two sensibly different answers. move2::mt_filter_per_interval() gives bucketed answer: divide time 45-minute windows (aligned wall-clock intervals via floor_date), pick one fix per window. criterion can "first", "last", "random". buckets aligned wall clock, actual time lag retained fixes guaranteed equal 45 minutes; first observed fix window falls 10:55 next 11:00, kept (belong different hour windows 5 minutes apart time).
code: leroy_45 <- mt_filter_per_interval(leroy, unit = "45 min",                                     criterion = "first") nrow(leroy); nrow(leroy_45) #> [1] 300 #> [1] 157 summary(mt_time_lags(leroy_45, units = "min")) #>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.     NAs  #>   14.28   15.10   37.48   51.06   45.00  779.53       1

title: Interpolating and thinning trajectories
text: mt_filter_per_interval() fine visualisation, quick-look downsampling, feeding method tolerant irregular sampling. mt_thin_time() solves stricter problem: find largest subset fixes every successive retained pair within [interval - tolerance, interval + tolerance]. answer longest path small DAG sorted timestamps; computed linear-time dynamic-programming sweep rather memoised recursion legacy implementation, scales cleanly + fixes. retained-lag distribution shows two regimes function produces construction: Within-run lags fall inside [interval - tolerance, interval + tolerance] — tolerance-admissible transitions DP maximised. -run lags exceed interval + tolerance — original gaps long bridge; run-splitter pre-pass decomposed track gaps thinning never pretends bridge . retained lag ever shorter interval - tolerance; hard contract function enforces. Tie-breaking several chains equally long: criterion = "closest" (default) — minimum summed deviation target interval, preferring chains hit target evenly. criterion = "first" — earliest-starting chain, matching legacy "first" behaviour.
code: thinned <- mt_thin_time(leroy,                          interval  = "30 min",                          tolerance = "5 min",                          remove    = TRUE) nrow(leroy); nrow(thinned) #> [1] 300 #> [1] 153  lags <- mt_time_lags(thinned, units = "min") summary(lags[!is.na(lags)]) #>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.  #>   28.35   29.78   30.08   52.30   30.47  794.25

title: Interpolating and thinning trajectories
text: “Give one fix every 300 metres travel” handled mt_thin_distance(). walks along track, accumulating great-circle (lon/lat) planar (projected) distance via move2::mt_distance(). Like time case, question two sensible answers, chosen method. default, method = "step", greedy one: keep first fix, keep fix time cumulative travel since last retained fix reaches distance. Every retained pair least distance travel apart. method = "interval" distance-space twin mt_thin_time(): finds largest subset every successive retained pair falls within [distance - tolerance, distance + tolerance] travel, using dynamic-programming sweep. Reach want spacing band rather floor. cases multi-track input thinned per individual output labelled place thin_selected column (matching mt_thin_time() convention). method = "step" first fix track always retained; method = "interval" longest-chain selection may start later. distance can numeric metre count units object (units::set_units(0.5, "km")), call can read naturally.
code: leroy_300m <- mt_thin_distance(leroy, distance = 300) nrow(leroy); sum(leroy_300m$thin_selected) #> [1] 300 #> [1] 79  ## filtered output for downstream use leroy_300m_kept <- mt_thin_distance(leroy, distance = 300, remove = TRUE) leroy_300pm30 <- mt_thin_distance(leroy, distance = 300, tolerance = 30,                                   method = "interval", remove = TRUE) nrow(leroy_300pm30) #> [1] 73

title: Utility Functions for Movement Data Based on move2
text: UD returned track’s CRS (lon/lat), track overlays directly. See vignette("UD_dbbmm_ud") full workflow.
code: library(move2) library(move2utils) library(terra) library(scales)  fishers <- mt_read(mt_example()) fishers <- fishers[!sf::st_is_empty(fishers), ] leroy   <- fishers[mt_track_id(fishers) == "M1", ]  ## Dynamic Brownian-bridge motion variance. `location_error` is the GPS ## error in metres; `window_size` / `margin` set the moving window for the ## variance breakpoint search (tune with `mt_suggest_dbbmm_window()`). var <- mt_dbbmm_variance(leroy, location_error = 25, window_size = 31, margin = 7) ud  <- mt_dbbmm_ud(var, dim_size = 600, ext = 1)        # isotropic UD raster vol <- ud_volume(ud)                                    # cumulative-volume space vol[vol[] > 0.99] <- NA                                 # keep the 99% range vol <- terra::trim(vol)                                 # crop to the occupied area  ## Directional (bivariate-Gaussian) variant. The directional kernel is ## elongated, so it needs a slightly larger `ext` to fit the raster. var_d <- mt_dbgb_variance(leroy, location_error = 25, window_size = 31, margin = 7) ud_d  <- mt_dbgb_ud(var_d, dim_size = 600, ext = 1.5) vol_d <- ud_volume(ud_d) vol_d[vol_d[] > 0.99] <- NA vol_d <- terra::trim(vol_d)  par(mfrow = c(2, 1)) plot(vol,   main = "dBBMM (isotropic)") plot(leroy, max.plot = 1, type = "l", add = TRUE, col = alpha("white", 0.5)) plot(vol_d, main = "dBGB (directional)") plot(leroy, max.plot = 1, type = "l", add = TRUE, col = alpha("white", 0.5))

text: tracks animal different speed regimes (resting colony + flight, wintering + migration, perched + foraging), per-fix detectors threshold dominant baseline distribution flag minority state’s fixes anomalous — even none GPS errors. Empirical example: Columba livia Saline-20160803-048308 (homing pigeon, n = 5479). pigeon two modes — perched loft (0.10 m/s) racing flight (15.2 m/s). naive defaults mt_clean_track() flags 696 fixes (12.7 %) — racing flight, GPS errors. Naive speed cap atlastools correctly flag 0 track racing flight biologically 30 m/s physiological cap. Symptoms: high flag rate (>5 %) track visible -trajectory fixes; mt_diagnose_clean_track() Panel 1 shows multiple substantive modes; Panel 2 shows sustained band elevated flag rate corresponding minority state. : see vignette(“OUTLIER_3_state_conditional”) — segment speed mode, run mt_clean_track() per segment, recombine. filter track one state cleaning.

what: Failure mode 2 — block-shaped contamination at naive defaults
title: Utility Functions for Movement Data Based on move2
text: tracks sustained contaminated trains (GPS spoofs, deployment confusion, multi-fix data corruption) auto-cap can land biologically absurd values (data’s outliers define “gap” auto-cap finds). speed primitive doesn’t fire spoof boundaries reliably enough block expansion seed, contaminated train silently kept. Empirical example: K02 golden eagle (real Movebank study 2830439412, n = 851 k, 175-fix spoof 2025-06-14). naive defaults mt_clean_track() recovers 0 / 175 spoof fixes (auto-cap landed 88 m/s, far biological eagle speed). (mass = 4.5, mode = "flying") wrapper recovers 175 / 175 via block expansion. Symptoms: final flags despite track obviously contaminated regions; wrapper now prints “primitive-disagreement signature” warning bridge caught flags conjunction dropped — supplying mass+mode resolves . : supply (mass, mode) mt_clean_track() (auto-derives Hirt 2017 physiological cap), pass v_max = <published_value> sprint-mode-aware species. wrapper also warns auto-cap lands 50 m/s.

title: Utility Functions for Movement Data Based on move2
text: Several methods ported onto move2 original descriptions. corridor concept follows LaPoint, Gallery, Wikelski & Kays (2013) Landscape Ecology 28: 1615–1630. dynamic Brownian-bridge utilisation distribution motion variance follow Horne, Garton, Krone & Lewis (2007) Ecology 88: 2354–2363 Kranstauber, Kays, LaPoint, Wikelski & Safi (2012) Journal Animal Ecology 81: 738–746, directional bivariate-Gaussian-bridge variant Kranstauber, Safi & Bartumeus (2014) Movement Ecology 2: 5. Utilisation distributions compared Earth mover’s distance (Rubner, Tomasi & Guibas 2000 International Journal Computer Vision 40: 99–121), computed via Sinkhorn optimal-transport approximation (Cuturi 2013 Advances Neural Information Processing Systems 26). outlier-detection framework — four complementary primitives (geometric bridge residual, path-vs-displacement detour ratio, probabilistic movement-metric, step-level speed cap) sharing gap-aware non-parametric normalisation combinable iterative unified detector evidence-corroborated flagging (default; class_aware rules selectable via consensus =) plus topological block expansion — novel scientific content package described companion paper (bioRxiv preprint, submitted Methods Ecology Evolution).

what: Is a CRS suitable for running the Brownian-bridge (dBBMM/dBGB) math directly? The kernel needs Euclidean distances in metres, so a CRS is suitable iff it is projected (not longitude/latitude) AND its linear unit is the metre. We deliberately do NOT second-guess a metric projection the user chose (e.g. flagging high-latitude web-Mercator distortion): trusting the user's projection is the contract for the legacy UD layer. A non-metre linear unit (e.g. US-feet) returns FALSE and routes through the AEQD path – correct numerics, just a resample at the end. — .crs_is_suitable

title: move2utils: Utility Functions for Movement Data Based on move2 — move2utils-package
text: Utility functions working animal movement data stored 'move2' objects. Four outlier-detection primitives provided, composable individually unified 'mt_clean_track()' entry-point: () geometric bridge-residual method scores fix deviation time-weighted Brownian-bridge mean temporal neighbours, leverage-immune construction, optional directional decomposition error-morphology classification; (ii) path-vs-displacement detour ratio scores fix dimensionless ratio cumulative path length chord displacement sliding window, time-insensitive scale-invariant; (iii) probabilistic method scores fix empirical joint distribution speed, angular velocity, gap-aware auto-differences, non-parametric gap-aware normalisation robust irregular sampling; (iv) step-level speed cap dip-test-validated data-driven default catches boundary transitions coherent outlier blocks per-fix detectors structurally resolve. State-aware bridge variants ('mt_flag_outliers_dbgb()', 'mt_flag_outliers_dbbmm()') estimate per-axis bridge motion variance flag fixes via envelope rule across three Z channels, useful behavioural states make single global threshold - -flag. package also provides dynamic Brownian bridge movement models (dBBMM) dynamic bivariate Gaussian bridge (dBGB) variance estimation utilisation-distribution computation, migrated 'move' package C kernels modern 'move2'/'sf'/'terra' spatial stack.

title: move2utils 0.2.0 — class-aware flagging architecture
text: New function mt_flag_outliers_dbgb() now canonical state- aware bridge primitive. estimates per-axis (parallel / orthogonal) motion variance via mt_dbgb_variance() applies envelope flag rule across three Z channels: bridge_z_para – residual component along local travel direction normalised parallel-axis sigma; |Normal(0,1)| bridge null. bridge_z_orth – across-axis component normalised orthogonal-axis sigma. bridge_z_chisq = sqrt(Z_para^2 + Z_orth^2) – diagonal-Sigma Mahalanobis magnitude; Rayleigh(1) null. Reduces dBBMM scalar Z sigma_para = sigma_orth. fix flagged three channels exceeds threshold, plus bridge_z_class diagnostic label tagging flagged fix channel(s) fired – including chisq-sub-classification axis dominance (isotropic_para_dom, isotropic_orth_dom, isotropic) directional information recoverable even joint Z fires. Threshold methods. z_threshold_method = "bonferroni" (default) applies per-channel parametric thresholds joint FWER <= 0.05 (alpha/2 chisq, alpha/4 per-axis channel). "bh_fdr" applies alpha allocation BH-FDR. "gap" runs package’s broken-stick + tail-decay inflection detector per channel (self-thresholding; useful diagnostic exploration mis- calibrates raw Z whose null half-normal / Rayleigh thin natural tails – see ?mt_flag_outliers_dbgb Details). Performance. Underlying dBGB variance estimation runs native C (src/bgb_var_window_c.c), bringing ~1.7x cost dBBMM (~200x slower previous -R implementation one optim() call per breakpoint candidate per window).
